purpose: Inventory of explicit top-level status_vocabulary objects in Source registers. No status terms or definitions are rewritten.
guard: Same spelling is not treated as same meaning unless definitions match exactly or a later research review maps them explicitly.

terms.definition: Named in Blaschka workshop or receiving-side evidence as participating in a specific transaction.
A surviving archive of the intermediary has been located, but the Blaschka transaction has not yet been isolated inside it.
The actor is securely named in the transaction but no dedicated archival fonds has yet been located.
A later or successor-company archive is historically connected but requires proof that earlier records were inherited.
A named personal and/or corporate archive survives as a collection of record.
No dedicated corporate fonds has been identified; the business must be reconstructed across workshop, customer, museum, and manuscript repositories.
The source explicitly concerns Blaschka models, catalogue, order, payment, agency, packing, shipment, receipt, breakage, or resale.
A customer or museum record explicitly documents transactions with the dealer but Blaschka content must be checked item by item.
Same-period business correspondence documenting the dealer's commercial practice without establishing a Blaschka transaction.
Dealer-business material after the marine-model production period; useful for institutional continuity and commercial practice only.
A substantial primary-source corpus is openly digitized with page images and/or downloadable OCR/text.
Collection identity and dates are verified, but letter content must be read before topic claims are assigned.
The displayed archival label and structured metadata date disagree; the manuscript/page label remains the authority until image review.
An individual BHL correspondence part has a separately downloadable PDF and persistent record on Zenodo, deposited by Plazi from BHL.
The archival unit explicitly names Blaschka or is a dedicated Blaschka archive.
Business archive of a documented Blaschka dealer or distributor.
Museum or institutional records explicitly document a Blaschka transaction, custody event or collection.

Archive is directly tied to a Blaschka-holding institution and contains the relevant class of acquisition, accession, correspondence or museum records, but the decisive Blaschka item remains to be isolated.
A named personal or institutional fonds is historically well positioned to close a known provenance gap, but a Blaschka-specific item has not yet been verified.
A named archive is tied to reported direct Blaschka evidence, but the decisive archival item still requires retrieval or shelfmark confirmation.
A named institutional series is directly positioned to test a documented Blaschka relationship, but the decisive item has not yet been isolated.
A named institutional archive is retained as a controlled comparison and is not itself treated as direct Blaschka evidence.
A receiving-side archive is strongly tied to a documented Blaschka transaction, but the decisive local record still requires retrieval.
A named personal fonds is well positioned to close a documented provenance or chronology gap, but a Blaschka-specific mention has not yet been verified.
Dealer business records are retained as controls for commercial practice but are not themselves direct Blaschka evidence.
